Unfortunately, regarding the definitions of this anomaly, known in stalker slang as "Greedy," scientists limit themselves only to vague hypotheses. The most popular of these states that it is a rift into some other dimension, and material objects from our universe undergo annihilation and conversion into nutritional energy. However, since the rift is truly small (in a metaphysical sense), it is impossible to pull a whole stalker through this "eye of a needle." Yet the suction force is quite high, so it feels as if something is holding him. Discarded objects can cause a certain collapse of this rift, which looks like the "saturation" of this anomaly's animal component.
A formation of a nature that is not fully understood. When a stalker enters the field of effect of this anomaly, a total change of the brain's psychophysical matrix occurs. Only basic motor and physiological functions are preserved; essentially, a person turns into a so-called "zombie." This type of brain damage cannot be treated.
A mythical artifact that seems to grow into a stalker's fate. The "Black Mark" cannot simply be thrown away or sold - it returns until passed to someone else. The mark slowly drains health and attracts the Zone's troubles; its sticky surface smells of damp earth and decay. They say people do not live long with it.
A formation of a nature not fully understood. Upon contact with the body, it inflicts injuries similar to the effects of strong acid. It forms three types of artifacts: "Slime," "Slug," and "Mica."
One of the first recorded anomalies. It inflicts strike damage with a variable gravitational field. The result of an encounter with a "Springboard" can vary—from minor bruises and contusions to instant death. During the daytime, it is easily detected by distortions in the air above the anomaly and swirling leaves. It is fixed by any type of detector, as well as by throwing various objects into it. It forms three types of artifacts: "Jellyfish," "Stone Flower," and "Night Star."
An anomalous formation about 3 meters in diameter that accumulates static electricity. When disturbed, the anomaly explodes with a dozen mini-lightnings, discharging for 2-3 seconds; the electric shock for any living creature is almost always fatal. A characteristic feature of "Electra" is the bluish mist visible over it during the day. It is detected by any type of detector or by throwing metal objects. It forms three types of artifacts: "Sparkler," "Flash," and "Moonlight."
Anomally mutated vegetation. Upon the rapid approach of a living creature, it releases a cloud of particles that, in case of contact with exposed or poorly protected skin, seriously injure the latter. It does not react to slowly moving objects. It forms three types of artifacts (possibly these are seeds): "Thorn," "Crystal Thorn," and "Urchin."
An anomaly of a presumably gravitational nature. At the moment of activation, it sucks in everything within a radius of 5-6 meters with terrible force. If you fall into the center of a "Vortex," there is practically no chance of survival: the body of both animal and human will be compressed into a tight lump and then torn apart at the moment of the so-called discharge. It can be detected by the characteristic movement of the air and leaves being pulled toward the center. It forms three types of artifacts: "Wrenched," "Gravi," and "Goldfish."
A gravitational anomaly harmless to health, allowing one to forget about the laws of gravity for a while. Within a local volume several meters in diameter, Earth's gravity is significantly reduced. It forms the "Pellicle" artifact.
The name is due to the effect of lifting any living creature into the air followed by spinning it up to enormous speeds. The nature of the "Whirligig" has not yet been fully researched. It is detected by a light dust vortex at a distance of 3-4 meters from the ground. It is very important not to miss the moment the pull into the anomalous vortex begins and not to enter the zone of maximum effect in the center—only then is there a chance to escape with minimal injuries. It forms three types of artifacts: "Stone Blood," "Meat Chunk," and "Soul."
A zone of increased level—more than 50 µR/h—of radiation. Prolonged stays in such places must be avoided.
An anomaly that can rightfully be called a small miracle: within a volume several meters in diameter, the flow of time slows down many times over. It apparently has no negative impact on health, but it is not easy to get out of it. Interestingly, in the center of the "Time Machine," the "Mama's beads" artifact is usually found; upon its removal, the anomaly ceases to exist.
In an inactive state, it looks like a barely visible cloud of hot air; however, when any object or living creature enters its range of effect, it forms a cone-shaped pillar of fire with a temperature of about 1500K. It forms three types of artifacts: "Droplet," "Fireball," and "Crystal."
"Compass" A rare artifact with chaotic formations that resemble needles. It points nowhere, but an electric discharge activates it and briefly drives the wearer's muscles. Then hunger arrives with a vengeance: the "Compass" takes the fuel for its work straight from the body.
The fully opened "Compass" gives the muscles a clear boost, while the artifact no longer burns calories or leaves the wearer ravenous.
A degenerated "Compass" artifact. Its needles have stopped, the discharge is gone, and its properties are lost.
"Pseudo-light"
The soft glow of "Pseudo-light" is deceptive. The artifact creates a thermal barrier and reduces damage from open flame, but it does not remove radiation or make the wearer safe from every anomaly. Its field is otherwise quiet. On the belt, the dry heat around the wearer seems to lose its bite, though the source itself remains dangerous.
"Gleam"
A close relative of "Flash" with a more stable structure. "Glint" absorbs explosion energy and takes the impact on itself, leaving a brief ozone trail around the wearer. Its field clings to the weapon's movements, but a long walk soon reminds the wearer of hunger.
"Storage Battery"
An exceptionally rare variety of the "Dummy" artifact. It absorbs and scatters powerful electrical discharges without noticeable side effects. Scientists suspect that the "Accumulator" does not destroy energy, but sends it somewhere beyond familiar space.
"Eye"
The "Eye" is born near the dual "Snow" anomaly. Its field lightens the carried load and protects against explosions, but gradually exhausts the wearer and makes them especially vulnerable to chemical burns. When brought to the sights, the field makes the view seem to drift a fraction behind the hand. Individual specimens differ in the strength of these effects.
The "Eye" with a thin field slightly lightens the load and catches part of an explosion wave. It also drains strength more fiercely than usual and offers poor protection against chemical burns. At the sights, the thin field makes the view lag noticeably behind the hand.
The "Eye" with an uneven field noticeably eases the pack and softens explosions, but still leaves the wearer exposed to chemically aggressive surroundings. At the sights, the field makes the picture reluctant to follow a quick correction.
The "Eye" with a dense field lightens the wearer well and noticeably dampens an explosion wave. Its secondary trace is weaker, but chemical vulnerability has not disappeared. At the sights, the dense field makes a steady correction feel heavy.
The fully opened "Eye" gives the maximum lightening effect and reliably softens explosions while barely draining the wearer's strength. Chemical vulnerability is noticeably weaker, though chemical burns are still dangerous. Even fully opened, the field leaves a faint delay in the view when the weapon is raised.
A degenerated "Eye" artifact. The field that lightened the load and dampened explosions has fallen apart; only a cloudy shell remains.

"Pizza" "Pizza", also called "Fried Eggs", got its name from its flat shape and mottled color. Its field slows metabolism and lets the wearer go without food for a long time. When it touches a charged battery, the artifact's edges begin to pulse as if waking and sharing their last warmth.
"Electric Beads" "Electric Beads" are a masterpiece of transmutation in "Snow", requiring the rarest trophies from the bodies of dangerous mutants. Even before activation, the "Beads" vibrate noticeably in the hand, and the air around them always carries a sharp smell of ozone and singed fur. The artifact creates a dense field around its bearer that seems to ignore electrical discharges and greatly softens bullet impacts, turning a stalker into a living fortress. Veteran stalkers also whisper of an unusual affinity between this artifact and the Tesla site...
The fully opened "Electric Beads" have a dense field that softens bullets and dampens electrical discharges, while the artifact begins to return energy to the wearer. Hunger may still wake after a raid. On Tesla, even a tired stalker may feel an invisible current carrying the next step forward.

Its unusual property appears when searching fallen zombified bodies: a sudden counterstrike may lose its force, as if the Zone itself guides the wearer's hand. Vodka still leaves the pack as usual, but its bite seems unable to find the wearer. Each such mercy wears the artifact down.
"Electro-sparkler" A rare mutation of the ordinary "Sparkler". "Electro-Sparkler" combines a weak but clean discharge with unusual stability and is therefore a trophy of status. It has little practical use, but traders gladly pay for this electrical rarity.
"Snowball" The "Snowball" artifact is practically never found in natural conditions and stands apart from other, more well-known and studied wonders of the Zone. Its main property lies in the ability to spawn a "Whirligig" anomaly when a strictly defined sequence of presses and touches to the artifact's surface is performed. Such manipulations are referred to in scientific circles as "activation of the artifact's hidden properties" or simply "activation." Activation can be performed only once, as the entire energy accumulated by the artifact is released during the birth of the anomaly, leading to its complete destruction.

The Duty faction cleared a small spot for their base on the outskirts of the Wild Territory and allows stalkers to rest here. It's a kind of oasis in the desert: no anomalies, no mutants. You can look for the entrance to an underground laboratory located somewhere around here, but no one has ever returned from there, and what hides within is not properly known to anyone.
A kind of waiting room for the Zone, the first place where rookies arrive to gradually settle in. A trader lives in a cellar behind the village near the army checkpoint—it's useful to talk to him. Poking around the checkpoint and getting caught by the soldiers is not wise: they have orders to shoot without warning; on the other hand, some are ready to become instantly kinder for money, especially if the commanders aren't around. Killing soldiers is highly discouraged, except in cases of a direct threat to life.
A massive technical graveyard: piles of radioactive junk were brought here after the first accident. There are remains of old buildings and mutants can be encountered. Here, just like near the perimeter itself, there are many rookies, and bandits hang around nearby, always looking for a fatter piece without much trouble. You can find a few artifacts, but it's better not to linger—there are more interesting places. The former nuclear power plant that everyone has heard of at least once. This is the very heart of the Zone. According to legends, somewhere there is a certain thing capable of granting any wish—they call it the Monolith.

The Exclusion Zone was lit up by a bright, almost unbearable light, and clouds could be seen starting to evaporate in the sky. After a moment of complete silence came the roar and an earthquake. People fell to the ground, covering their eyes and ears; those who could, ran for their lives. From the outside, it looked as if all the nuclear fuel buried under the sarcophagus had blown up at once. A day later, government troops had already completely cordoned off the new Zone. With the help of satellites, it was discovered that the epicenter of the explosion was not at the power plant units themselves, but a kilometer away from them. It is believed that the entire station staff died instantly, but many other people remained inside the cordon ring. It was not possible to organize rescue operations, as the squads of people and equipment sent deep into the affected territory perished almost immediately. Sometime after the accident, the diameter of the Zone increased sharply by several kilometers. Most of the government troops guarding the perimeter and the scientific laboratories located there died instantly. Panic began; residents of surrounding villages and towns were evacuated in haste or fled on their own. A danger loomed over the world, the magnitude of which can still only be guessed at.
Two years have passed since the terrible catastrophe occurred in the Exclusion Zone around the Chernobyl NPP. A large number of dead and missing people, fallen livestock, blackened buildings, mutilated forest... scientists still cannot provide explanations for what happened. Meanwhile, the Zone, inside which completely fantastic anomalies were discovered, is growing. Rare expeditions encounter mutated species of animals with amazing characteristics.
Following in the footsteps of desperate lone stalkers, scientific expeditions are again taking up the large-scale study of the Zone. However, inside the army-guarded perimeter, there are already many "unaccounted for persons," ranging from poachers to bandits. For the most part, stalkers travel through the Zone in search of various anomalous formations, so-called artifacts, for which they often receive good money.
Army units, including special forces led by military stalker squads, undertook a major expedition into the Zone with the aim of breaking through to the CNPP and destroying the presumed cause of the deadly anomalous fields, or finally obtaining reliable information about the processes occurring there. This enterprise, in which more than a thousand people and much equipment took part, failed completely. Individual groups of survivors settled in the territory of the Zone without much hope of rescue. What is it — the Zone? What is the Zone? For some, it is a source of inexplicable wonders and wealth; for others, it is a mortal wound on the body of the Earth. Scientists argue about its nature: is it a result of a breakthrough in the noosphere, a physical manifestation of human subconsciousness, or simply a monstrous laboratory under the open sky? About teleports
Fanat:\nTeleports? Hell if I know what they are or how they work. I think of it like a hole in the wall to the neighbor's apartment. It's inconvenient, and you don't know where you'll end up or who you'll meet there—but hey, it's fast.\nGetting a teleport to work isn't that hard, in principle—you just need to know the "special" spot and have an artifact that allows you to break through that invisible "wall" in that specific location. But making that teleport work exactly how you need it to... for that, you have to account for a ton of factors: precise timing, air humidity, wind direction and strength... A whole lot of things. Don't overthink it. You also need a special gut feeling, and that's not something you can calculate...
About weapon wear
Lisaped:\nWhy does gear wear down so fast? Hm... Sit down, pour yourself a drink. Easy with the hands, you're spilling more than you're pouring...\nMany ask themselves this question about the wear and tear. I only ever heard a sensible answer from one scientist, a guy named Vasilyev... Good man, even if he was a "big head." Didn't shun stalkers, could knock back a glass of vodka without flinching, and explained things in a way that made sense... Well, almost.\nAnyway, I asked him. He says that time is also made of these tiny atoms—he gave 'em a name, but sorry, I can't repeat it. Those very atoms of time are always with us, so we don't notice 'em. Kind of like air. But here in the Zone, new time atoms appeared, ones not from our world. We barely notice them either. But! Only as long as our speed is low. Like a breeze. Or like sticking your head out of a fast car—it'll mess up your hair...\nKeep pouring, keep pouring...\nBut a bullet—its speed is even higher. So that bullet collides with "other" time much more. It ages in mid-flight, you could say. That's why hitting a target further than two hundred meters in the Zone is impossible... and the barrel gets a dose of this "wrong" time because of the bullet's high-speed flight. That's why the wear is so wild...\nThose foreign guns, and even our newer ones—they just fall apart after a dozen shots... But the Kalashnikov—it holds up, no problem...
About Mercenary goals Volkodav:\nAh! It's you again. You're starting to cross our path a little too often. You've got a very convenient alibi—I don't remember anything, I don't know anything. It seems to me that such experience doesn't just appear out of nowhere, eh? Who are you working for? Won't say? Well, well... Calm down. I won't tell you who I work for either... Professional ethics.\nWhat I'm getting at is: think about it, maybe we're looking for something similar—you and I. Your "legend" is handy—you can slip in anywhere quietly, ask about anything, and no one wonders: "Why are you hanging around here, searching?" Let's help each other; I've had enough of this Zone. These mutants, the anomalies, the idiots with guns who just want to shoot... I just want to finish the job quickly, and get back to a normal life, a warm toilet, healthy food, girls ready for anything...\nWhat job? Hm.. Alright. Basically, have you heard about the Monolithians? You know, those fanatics who have north and south mixed up in their heads. Lately, they've got new, unusual guns. Almost a hundred percent accuracy, and the stopping power, mama mia! Some corporations abroad would love to "ride the wave" and outdo their competitors in terms of supplying such weaponry. But here's the paradox, the gun exists, it kills, but it's impossible to take! Not even with any grabbers. You try to take it, and—poof, nothing but black smoke... So we're looking for any lead that would allow us to take such a weapon out of the Zone and take it apart, so to speak. Understand the principle.\nLook, if you find out anything, we won't stay in your debt—you'll be living like a king for a hundred years, I'm telling you for sure. There must be a solution! About PDA operation Docent:\nGlad to see you again. How do our PDAs work? They work fine. They have a communication program in them, in English it's called "Meeting Point." Voice communication is very unstable, but short text messages on a selected channel or, say, other information can be sent. The fact that the connection sometimes works over quite long distances is due to the anomalous influence of the Zone. No one has figured this out exactly yet. Personally, I think that under the influence of Emissions, the local space of our world mixes with the space of another world. And ultra-high frequencies, which have very small wavelengths, sometimes pass through the gaps between our dimension and another.\nSidorovich said that when they took the pilot batch of PDAs, they didn't think they could be used for communication. Just for local calculations. But that's how it turned out. And now a stalker is not entirely alone in this world and can sometimes even hope for help in a critical situation. Or, at least, send out a final farewell...

Possessing strong pharmaceuticals and radio-electronics, plus an unlimited amount of human material in concentration camps, the Nazis managed to achieve great success in creating psychotropic drugs and psychotronic installations. By the end of the war, they were close to implementing parallel consciousness and creating super-agents following embedded programs via verbal commands or visual images. Most of the work was carried out in Western Germany, and the research results fell into the hands of the Americans, who significantly developed them during the Cold War. In the Soviet Union, theoretical research was conducted at the Bekhterev Brain Institute, while practical research took place in secret NKVD, KGB, and GRU laboratories.\n...In the early eighties, Laboratory X-16 was established, and a successful attempt was made to create a biological cyber-system—an artificial brain—where behavioral algorithms of artificially implanted parallel consciousness were modeled with the forced blocking of specific memory sectors. The test subject's brain was connected to a bio-computer via a telepathic channel, and a personality matrix replacement was performed, altering the individual's persona. The procedure was tested on guards and civilian personnel under the guise of medical examinations, kept strictly secret so that no one would even suspect it. Hundreds of special agents with unknown missions are now waiting for a code signal to begin executing their embedded programs.\n...In 2012, during the first Emission after the 1986 accident when the Zone first appeared, the bio-computer, the artificial brain, began to show signs of non-humanoid xeno-intelligence. Initially, this was met with enthusiasm; a new self-consciousness was created whose power could be used to acquire new knowledge. But things did not turn out as intended. Academician Patonov was the first to identify the problem. In his article, he pointed out strange patterns between the consequences of Emissions and the activity of the bio-computer.
